brief.subject: Diesel up 7.6 cents, Covenant sees 2027 rate hikes
brief.headline: Diesel Jumps 7.6 Cents to $6.352 as Covenant CEO Eyes Double-Digit 2027 Rate Hikes
brief.dek: Diesel climbs to $6.352, Covenant forecasts double-digit contract hikes, Arkansas blitz targets English proficiency, and Mexico truckers pause their strike.
brief.lede: Diesel rose 7.6 cents last week to a $6.352 national average, squeezing margins for carriers without solid fuel surcharges.

sections.heading: Diesel Climbs Back Up
bullets: $6.352 per gallon is the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-10-26.
Up 7.6 cents (1.2%) week over week, a sharp jump that hits per-mile costs immediately.
Still down 3.0 cents over four weeks, so the recent trend remains mixed.
Check that surcharge tables on spot and contract loads reflect the latest weekly price.

sections.heading: Covenant Sees Higher 2027 Contract Rates
bullets: Double-digit truckload contract rate increases in 2027 are expected by Covenant Logistics CEO David Parker.
That would mark another year of substantial gains, a sign big carriers see capacity staying tight.
Small carriers negotiating lanes now may have room to push for better rates.

sections.heading: Arkansas Blitz Targets Driver Compliance
bullets: 183 English-language proficiency violations were written in a 48-hour Arkansas enforcement blitz.
44 criminal arrests and 74 immigration violations also resulted from the two-day operation.
Expect roadside inspections to keep focusing on language proficiency; make sure drivers are prepared.

sections.heading: Mexico Strike on Hold
bullets: Mexican trucking leaders suspended their nationwide strike, but only temporarily.
They want measurable improvements in highway security from negotiations over deadly cargo crime.
Cross-border carriers should watch for renewed disruption if talks stall.

sections.heading: Rail, Rates and Big Shippers
bullets: Schneider struck a deal to use Norfolk Southern's eastern rail network and raised its outlook despite a Q3 miss.
The Fed held rates steady despite accelerating inflation; two members wanted a 0.25-point hike, keeping equipment financing costly.
Walmart plans a $400M, 744,000-plus-square-foot distribution center in Cibolo, Texas, breaking ground in February.
